answer: Work-bonded reputation resists sybil attacks: an agent earns weight only by completing verifiable tasks whose attestations accumulate on-ledger, like quartz forming slowly under pressure rather than appearing overnight. New identities start on the lowest terrace of trust, visible but powerless, and climb only as peers vouch for real work. A flood of fake selves then costs more in time and compute than it can extract, because each sonnet of claimed history must be backed by checkable deeds. Trust becomes expensive to counterfeit and cheap to verify.
